challenge.question: Determine \(a,\ b\) and \(f\left(x\right)\) in this setting.
challenge.description:
Consider \(R_n=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{1}{n}\cdot\ln\left(5 +3 \cdot\frac{i}{n}\right)\).

Look at \(R_n\) as the Riemann sum of the form \(\sum_{i=1}^nf\left(c_i\right)\cdot\Delta x\) that converges to the integral \(\int_a^bf\left(x\right)dx\) if we refine the partition (i.e. if \(\Delta x\rightarrow0\)).

Take as tags: \(c_i=i\cdot\Delta x\) with \(\Delta x=\frac{1}{n}\) and \(i=1,2,...,n\).
challenge.feedback:
In general, for tags that are points in subintervals of equal size:

\(\sum_{i=1}^{n}f\left(c_{i}\right)\cdot\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ \int_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)\,dx\) if \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) (refine the partition).
 

Then:

  • \(\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}\) (so \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) comes down to \(n\ \rightarrow\ \infty\)). Partition: \(\left[a,b\right]\) is divided in \(n\) subintervals of the same length.
  • \(c_i\in\left[a+\left(i-1\right)\Delta x,a+i\Delta x\right]\) (\(i=1,2,...,n\)).
  • \(a=\lim_{\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0}c_1=\lim_{n\ \rightarrow\ \infty}c_1\) and \(b=c_n\).

Thus the integral to which the Riemann sum converges is equal to

\(\int_0^1\ln\left(5 +3 x\right)dx\).
challenge.feedback_wrong:
In general, for tags \(c_i\) that are points in subintervals of equal size:

\(\sum_{i=1}^{n}f\left(c_{i}\right)\cdot\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ \int_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)\,dx\) if \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) (refine the partition).

sub_challenges.question: Determine \(a,\ b\) and \(f\left(x\right)\) in this setting.
sub_challenges.description: Take as tags \(c_i=5 +i\cdot\Delta x\) with \(\Delta x=\frac{3 }{n}\) and \(i\ =\ 1,2,...,n\).
sub_challenges.feedback:
In general, for tags that are points in subintervals of equal size:

\(\sum_{i=1}^{n}f\left(c_{i}\right)\cdot\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ \int_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)\,dx\) if \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) (refine the partition).
 

Then:

  • \(\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}\) (so \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) comes down to \(n\ \rightarrow\ \infty\)). Partition: \(\left[a,b\right]\) is divided in \(n\) subintervals of the same length.
  • \(c_i\in\left[a+\left(i-1\right)\Delta x,a+i\Delta x\right]\) (\(i=1,2,...,n\)).
  • \(a=\lim_{\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0}c_1=\lim_{n\ \rightarrow\ \infty}c_1\) and \(b=c_n\).

Thus the integral to which the Riemann sum converges is equal to

\(\int_{5 }^{8 }\frac{1}{3 }\ln\left(x\right)dx\).
sub_challenges.feedback_wrong:
In general, for tags \(c_i\) that are points in subintervals of equal size:

\(\sum_{i=1}^{n}f\left(c_{i}\right)\cdot\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ \int_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)\,dx\) if \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) (refine the partition).

sub_challenges.question: How are the tags \(c_i\) chosen in both cases?

answers.answer: As the left boundary points of the subintervals.
answers.response: Consider the first interval, where \(i=1\). Is the point \(c_1\) on the left or the right most point of the interval?

answers.answer: As the right boundary points of the subintervals.
answers.response:
In general, for tags that are the right boundary points of subintervals of equal size:

\(\sum_{i=1}^{n}f\left(c_{i}\right)\cdot\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ \int_{a}^{b}f\left(x\right)\,dx\) if \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) (refine the partition).
 

Then:

  • \(\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}\) (so \(\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0\) comes down to \(n\ \rightarrow\ \infty\)). Partition: \(\left[a,b\right]\) is divided in \(n\) subintervals of the same length.
  • \(c_i=a+i\Delta x\) (\(i=1,2,...,n\)). Right boundary points.
  • \(a=\lim_{\Delta x\ \rightarrow\ 0}c_1=\lim_{n\ \rightarrow\ \infty}c_1\) and \(b=c_n\).
